wait wait i asked a simple question about my data if it was larger dataset then those metrics will be more diverse isnt it

Not necessarily! In fact, having a larger dataset wouldn't automatically make accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score more diverse or widely separated. 

Those metrics measure different aspects of performance (e.g., precision looks at false positives, recall looks at false negatives), but they naturally converge when:
1. **The dataset classes are balanced** (like your `species` column, which has nearly equal counts for `Iris-setosa`, `Iris-versicolor`, and `Iris-virginica`). 
2. **The model makes very few errors** (in your test set of 30 samples, the Random Forest only misclassified 1 sample). 

When a model is this accurate on balanced data, every metric approaches 100% (or ~96.67% in your case), keeping them tightly grouped regardless of whether you have 150 rows or 150,000 rows. Metrics only diverge significantly when a dataset is heavily imbalanced or when a model struggles with specific classes (e.g., high precision but very low recall due to lots of false negatives).
